source: OpenCode Zen API + provider documentation + benchmarks + https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/#privacy

selection_rules.output_limit_rule: For subagents that must EMIT large payloads (review lens JSON, spec/tasks reports), the binding model parameter is output_limit (max output tokens per response), NOT context_window. context_window only bounds how much INPUT fits; output_limit is what a finish: "length" death exhausts. When output_limit is too small, the model burns its whole budget reasoning and emits nothing (the provider stops with finish reason "length" — reproduced locally). Historical failure: opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free at output 32000 exhausted its reasoning budget before emitting any output.
selection_rules.threshold_rationale: Both thresholds derive from the observed 32000-token finish=length failure on large structured payloads: general_large_payload (64000) is the warning zone for any subagent emitting large payloads, at 2x that failure; role_minimums.review (128000) is 4x the failure baseline, the floor for review-lens JSON payloads once reasoning overhead is counted. Code reads ONLY selection_rules.thresholds; prose in this file must not restate these numbers independently of the object.
selection_rules.large_payload_threshold: Models whose output_limit is below thresholds.general_large_payload must NOT be selected for subagents that emit large structured payloads (review lenses, reports); generate-agent-config.sh warns before such an assignment. The numeric value lives only in thresholds.general_large_payload — code reads that key, not this prose.
selection_rules.role_selection: select_role_model applies one criteria-driven path to every role (role_aliases resolved first). Candidates are the free ids in .models (opencode/big-pickle and ids ending in -free) whose numeric privacy_tier prefix is <= the max_tier argument (a missing privacy_tier counts as the highest tier) and whose output_limit >= the role's minimum: thresholds.role_minimums[role] when the registry defines one, else thresholds.general_large_payload. Candidates sort privacy tier ascending, then output_limit descending, then context_window descending, then id ascending — the first one wins. When no candidate qualifies, selection falls back to role_chains[role] (or role_chains.default), taking the first entry that is free, present in .models, and tier-eligible; chains keep their opencode/big-pickle terminal append and are ordered fallback lists only, never the primary ranking. If nothing qualifies either way, select_role_model echoes NONE and still returns 0. All numeric values live only in thresholds — code reads that object, not this prose.
selection_rules.limits_reverify: Re-verify limits: daily-check.sh now performs this automatically — on every run it fetches https://models.dev/api.json, applies verified context_window/output_limit to models newly added to the registry at add time, and prints a yellow advisory when an existing entry has drifted (existing entries are never auto-corrected by the daily run). The manual procedure below remains the offline fallback: fetch https://models.dev/api.json and compare context_window/output_limit for every model referenced by role_chains against the registry entries; refresh last_updated with the check date. Run it when a new model appears on Zen and at least quarterly, or whenever the automated check cannot reach the source, so the corrected limits cannot go silently stale.
selection_rules.privacy_source: https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/#privacy — the Privacy section lists the models whose data may be used to improve or train models, and states zero-retention + no training for every model not in that exception list. daily-check.sh classifies privacy from that page at add time (writing the tier, the verbatim matched statement as evidence, and this URL) and reports tier drift on every daily run as a yellow advisory only. A tier may only be raised on an affirmative statement on that page; absence of evidence keeps the model at its current tier (fail-closed) — absence of evidence is not evidence. Manually verify this page whenever the docs change or whenever the automated check cannot reach them.

1_strict.label: Strict Privacy
1_strict.description: No data used for training. Zero-retention. No logging for improvement.

2_anonymous_improvement.label: Anonymous Improvement Only
2_anonymous_improvement.description: Data may be logged for service improvement but NOT linked to your identity. No model training.

3_model_improvement.label: Model Improvement
3_model_improvement.description: Data may be used to improve the model during the free period. Not linked to identity.

4_explicit_training.label: Explicit Training
4_explicit_training.description: Data is explicitly used to train future models. You consent to this by using the service.
